title: Stock Reconciliation performance and validation issues with large data (500+ warehouses, 20k+ rows)

posts.cooked:
Description

Stock Reconciliation in ERPNext becomes impractical in large implementations due to multiple issues:

  1. Performance Issue

    • Submitting a reconciliation with 5000+ items takes 10–15 minutes or more.
    • With 500+ warehouses, reconciliation files often exceed 20,000 rows, which the system cannot handle.
    • Browser becomes unresponsive and server requests time out.

  2. Error Handling Issue

    • If multiple rows are invalid, ERPNext validates them one by one.
    • After a long wait, only one error is displayed.
    • Users must fix one error, re-submit, wait again, and repeat → very inefficient.

  3. Concurrency Limitation

    • Currently, only a single Stock Reconciliation can be submitted at a time.
    • This makes the process very lengthy for large datasets.

Steps to Reproduce

  1. Create a Stock Reconciliation with >5000 line items.
  2. Submit the document → takes 10–15 minutes, sometimes fails.
  3. Add multiple invalid rows → only one error is shown after long wait.
  4. Try to submit another reconciliation in parallel → blocked or impractical.

Expected Behavior

  • ERPNext should efficiently handle large reconciliations (5000+ items, 20k+ rows).
  • All validation errors should be shown at once.
  • Multiple Stock Reconciliations should be processed reliably without excessive delays.

Actual Behavior

  • Submission takes 10–15 minutes or fails.
  • Only one error is shown after long validation.
  • Reconciliations cannot be managed efficiently when data is very large.

Impact

  • Go-live stock adjustments with hundreds of warehouses and thousands of SKUs are not feasible.
  • Users waste significant time fixing errors one by one.
  • Overall process becomes unmanageable in enterprise-scale scenarios.

Suggested Improvements

  • Handle large reconciliations via background jobs.
  • Split commits into batches instead of one huge transaction.
  • Optimize child table/grid rendering for 20k+ rows.
  • Change validation logic to show all errors in a single run.
  • Improve concurrency handling to allow large-scale stock reconciliations without blocking.

Additional Question:
For organizations with huge datasets (e.g., 500+ warehouses and 20,000+ opening stock rows), what is the recommended best practice to upload opening stock in ERPNext?

  • Stock Reconciliation struggles with large files (5,000+ rows).
  • Splitting warehouse-wise still results in thousands of rows and is hard to manage.
  • Is there another scalable recommended approach (e.g., Utility or background jobs, etc.) officially advised for enterprise-scale opening stock uploads?

posts.name: Sambhaji Kolate
posts.cooked:
Can you share what error you are facing?

Generally, we do one warehouse at a time and category-wise Stock Reconciliation.

If row count is more than 100 and the system is simultaneously processing Sales Invoices or Sales Orders for the same items, there may be timeout due to database locks. but again it can be fixed by adding validation on blocking invoicing when Stock Reconciliation is going on for that item

Also I will suggest to use Stock Entry of type Material Receipt for opening stock, as well as instead of Stock Reconciliation, make a stock entry for difference qty

There are no simultaneous Sales Orders, Invoices, or other transactions happening at the time of opening stock upload. Since this is during go-live, we are first uploading the stock opening warehouse-wise.

The challenge we are facing is that a single warehouse itself has more than 15–20k rows. When we try to upload this much data in one Stock Reconciliation, the browser becomes unresponsive or, on submit, it throws an error saying that the file size exceeds the maximum allowed limit.

posts.name: Sambhaji Kolate
posts.cooked:
How many rows do you expect for real stock inspection, where a person physically counts inventory and updates the system?

If it’s just a one-time opening stock, you can write a script to make opening stock reconciliation. (bench console / system console)

You can also use the data import tool for stock reconciliation. Data import will create a separate entry for each item + warehouse combination, and per data import you can keep 5-10k rows.

We have already created Stock Reconciliations for opening using the Data Import tool, but still, whenever the submission has more than 5k rows, it is not working properly.

Also, you mentioned writing a script for opening entries - could you please clarify for what specific purpose I should write this script? Is it to bypass the limitations of Stock Reconciliation submission, or to directly create stock entries in the backend in smaller batches?

posts.name: Sambhaji Kolate
posts.cooked:
• If you need to process 15,000 records in ERPNext, you can:
    • Option 1: Create one Stock Reconciliation entry per item. This distributes the workload and helps avoid performance issues.
    • Option 2: Import all 15,000 records as Stock Reconciliation entries using the Data Import tool, and then submit them using a system console script or server-side script.

This approach helps maintain system performance and prevents validation errors when handling large datasets.
